speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing that. To better understand your condition, can you tell me how long you've been experiencing the swelling in your right knee?

speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Hemophilia A (Factor VIII deficiency) presenting with spontaneous hemarthrosis. The age (18 months), onset after minor trauma (playing), absence of direct injury, and strong maternal family history (X-linked recessive pattern) are classic for a bleeding disorder. I am requesting coagulation studies (PT, PTT, Factor VIII levels) and an MRI of the right knee to confirm the diagnosis and assess joint damage.
